questions.question: A code of ethics is best described as:
options: A list of punishments for dishonest staff
A formal statement of the values and standards of behaviour a business commits itself to
A legal contract with SARS
The rules for balancing a trial balance

questions.question: Why does Accounting specifically depend on ethics?
options: Accountants handle more money than other workers
Ethics is examinable, so it must be learned
Financial information only has value if it can be trusted — bent records stop being information
The law requires a code before a business may open

questions.question: The relationship between internal control and ethics is that:
options: They are the same thing under two names
Ethics replaces the need for controls in honest businesses
Controls matter only in big businesses; ethics only in small ones
Controls make dishonesty difficult; ethics makes it unwanted — a business needs both

subtopics.title: The Seven Characteristics, Defined for Marks

questions.question: Consistent adherence to rules and procedures, even under pressure, is:
options: Discipline
Transparency
Sustainability
Leadership

questions.question: A manager who explains a loss to the owner rather than burying it demonstrates:
options: Fairness
Accountability — answering for decisions and actions
Responsible management only
Discipline only

questions.question: Conducting business so it can endure — refusing profit today that destroys tomorrow's base — defines:
options: Transparency
Leadership
Sustainability
Accountability

questions.question: Why do ethics scenarios often admit more than one characteristic?
options: The characteristics overlap by design — the skill is choosing and defending the best fit
The syllabus is inconsistent
Only one answer is ever marked correct
Because scenarios are written vaguely by mistake

subtopics.title: Ethics Under Pressure — the Scenarios That Matter

questions.question: An owner instructs the bookkeeper to omit cash sales 'to reduce tax'. The owner's clearest breaches are:
options: Sustainability and discipline
Leadership (dishonesty instructed from the top) and fairness (the tax burden shifts to honest taxpayers)
Responsible management only
None — tax planning is always legal

questions.question: Re-pricing expired stock to sell quickly without disclosure chiefly breaches:
options: Transparency and fairness — the buyer cannot see what is really being sold
Discipline and leadership
Accountability only
No characteristic — pricing is the owner's right

questions.question: The lesson's pattern behind ethical failures is:
options: They happen only in large companies
They are usually accidents
A small, certain, immediate gain purchased with a large, delayed loss — and trust does not restock
They always break the law

subtopics.title: The Exam Method for Ethics Questions

questions.question: The four moves of an ethics answer, in order, are:
options: Quote GAAP, name a party, add a law, conclude
Define all seven characteristics, pick two, summarise, moralise
Consequence first, then the issue, then the name
State the issue plainly; name the characteristic(s); argue the link to the scenario; give consequence and correction

questions.question: 'This behaviour is wrong and very bad for everyone' earns nothing because:
options: It moralises without naming and applying a characteristic
It is too short
Ethics answers must never judge behaviour
The word 'bad' is banned

questions.question: Listing 'transparency, accountability, fairness' without tying each to the scenario fails because:
options: Only one characteristic may ever be named
Naming without applying earns little — each name must connect to a fact of the scenario
The list is in the wrong order
Lists are not allowed in Accounting

questions.question: The captain who trains hardest and never asks the team for anything they will not do themselves shows:
options: Fairness
Sustainability
Leadership — the example set from the front
Transparency

questions.question: Explaining team selections openly instead of whispering in corners is:
options: Transparency
Discipline
Responsible management
Accountability

questions.question: Refusing to win by injuring opponents 'because next season still has to be played' captures:
options: Accountability
Sustainability — never winning today in a way that poisons tomorrow
Discipline
Fairness only

questions.question: The shop that checks the till, finds your extra R50 and pays it out passes the tests of:
options: Sustainability and leadership
Discipline only
Accountability, fairness — and transparency, because the till could be checked at all
No characteristic — it is just good service

questions.question: A 'cash price, no paper' deal is designed to defeat which characteristic first?
options: Transparency — the deal is built to be invisible, with accountability lost alongside it
Sustainability
Discipline
Leadership

questions.question: Why should the spaza owner refuse the stock that 'fell off a truck', in business terms?
options: Stolen goods are always poor quality
The bargain is too small to matter
Suppliers dislike competition
The shop's real asset is the street's trust — one bargain today against the shop's whole name tomorrow

subtopics.title: Why Good Ethics Is Good Business

questions.question: Honest records convert into a business advantage because:
options: They reduce the need for stock
They can be shown to a bank — honest records get loans that shoeboxes never will
They make the shop look busy
SARS pays rewards for neat books

questions.question: The lesson compares discovered dishonesty to a compounding debt because:
options: Interest is charged on stolen money
Fines double every year
One discovered lie makes every past figure suspect — trust is not re-extended halfway
Banks compound everything

questions.question: The strongest structure for a 'discuss the importance of a code of ethics' answer is:
options: Ethics protects against the costs of dishonesty AND earns the profits of being trusted — characteristics named and tied to advantages
A list of the seven characteristics with definitions only
A story about a dishonest business
A single sentence stating ethics is important
